narrativeReportMd:
# Account R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Account has one clear local hard instance-breaking change: R4 `Account.partOf` was removed and replaced by R6 `Account.parent`. R6 also adds substantial optional Account content for billing status, episode coverage, diagnoses, procedures, guarantor financial detail, currency, balances, and calculation time. These additions do not invalidate existing R4 Account instances, but they create meaningful R6-to-R4 round-trip and generated-model risks.

## Scope
The assessment compared the supplied R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition-Account.json` files, package identity metadata, package index entries, and directly relevant local terminology artifacts. Inherited changes from DomainResource, Resource, Element, Extension, BackboneElement, and primitive/base datatypes are excluded from findings and listed as out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The main R4-to-R6 migration issue is a property rename/removal for account hierarchy: `partOf` must be transformed to `parent`. The main R6-to-R4 issue is that R6 Account can now carry much richer billing and clinical-billing context that R4 Account has no native place to store. Generated models also need updates for `description` changing from `string` to `markdown`, and consumers should no longer assume each guarantor always names a `party`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `Account:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:Account.partOf:7a6a56`: strict R6 validation will reject R4 instances that still contain `partOf`, and strict R4 validators will reject R6 instances that use `parent` unless converted.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for choosing lossless cross-version mappings for the new R6 billing/clinical fields and for confirming whether local business rules should treat the R6 Account subject commentary as a policy change.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most R6 additions were made as optional elements, which is backward-compatible for R4-to-R6 validation. The `partOf` rename is the avoidable local break; preserving `partOf` as an alias/deprecated element or adding `parent` while retaining `partOf` for one release would have reduced disruption.

## Follow-up analysis
Base resource/datatype changes, terminology expansions, Account search parameters, and rendered narrative change notes should be reviewed separately if a complete cross-version migration plan is needed.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Account keeps its artifact identity, but has a local hard break because `Account.partOf` was removed/replaced by `Account.parent`. The largest migration concerns are hierarchy-field transformation, R6-only billing/clinical/balance content that cannot round-trip to R4 without extensions or loss, and runtime assumptions around `description` typing and guarantor party requiredness. The main uncertainty is rationale/intent because no official diff or narrative change note was supplied.
summary.migrationThemesMd: R4-to-R6 migration should explicitly map `partOf` to `parent`, update generated models for the changed and added fields, and review validation of Account hierarchy data. R6-to-R4 conversion needs policy decisions for optional R6-only content: drop it, carry it in extensions, map to related resources such as Encounter/Condition/Procedure/Coverage/Claim where appropriate, or reject records requiring lossless round-trip. Business logic should also be tested for guarantors without `party` and for Account subjects that intentionally differ from clinical-resource patients.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition changes because the local R4 and R6 snapshots/differentials were compared directly and the package indexes confirm the same canonical Account artifact. Confidence is medium for semantic intent and terminology completeness because rendered narrative, official diffs, Jira/change notes, and live terminology expansions were not available.

findings.title: Account hierarchy element changed from partOf to parent

oldState.summary: R4 used optional `Account.partOf` to reference a parent Account.
oldState.narrativeMd: `Account.partOf` was a local optional reference to another Account and was the R4 native representation for account hierarchy.

newState.summary: R6 removes `Account.partOf` and adds optional `Account.parent` for the same account hierarchy role.

semanticText.short: Reference to an associated parent Account
semanticText.definition: Reference to an associated parent Account which has this account as a sub-account.

newState.narrativeMd: `Account.parent` is the R6 local field for the parent Account relationship. The target type and cardinality match the removed R4 element, but the wire name and generated property name changed.

facts.note: `Account.partOf` exists in R4 and is absent from R6 Account.
`Account.parent` is absent from R4 and exists in R6 Account.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The removed and added elements have the same parent path, cardinality, type, and Account target profile, and both describe a parent Account relationship. This is best treated as a rename/replacement rather than unrelated removal/addition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format and generated-property break. An R4 Account instance containing `partOf` has an element that is not defined in the R6 Account StructureDefinition. Conversely, an R6 Account using `parent` is not valid R4 content unless transformed. Generated models, FHIRPath expressions, JSON serializers, database columns, and search/index logic that reference `partOf` must be updated or bridged.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing account hierarchy can change billing roll-up, sub-account grouping, and responsibility workflows even though it is not a clinical safety element.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify the hierarchical parent-account relationship using a more direct element name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `Account.partOf` with clearer wording, or add `parent` while keeping `partOf` deprecated during transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of clarifying the account hierarchy as a parent/sub-account relationship is reasonable, but the R4 and R6 elements have the same cardinality, type, target, and role. The available evidence makes this primarily a wire-name and generated-property rename, so the hard instance and codegen break was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have kept `Account.partOf` and improved its short/definition to say it identifies the parent Account. If `Account.parent` was strongly preferred, R6 could have retained `partOf` as a deprecated synonym for at least one release and added an invariant or guidance discouraging both fields on the same instance. That duplication has real cleanup risk, but the simpler option of retaining the old field name would preserve R4 instances with low long-term cost.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping only `partOf` preserves compatibility but leaves a less direct name; keeping both names risks duplicate same-resource representations that may persist indefinitely.

evidence.quote: Reference to an associated parent Account which has this account as a sub-account.

evidence.detail: `Account.partOf` is absent from the R6 Account snapshot.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments are illustrative and include only the fields needed to show the hierarchy rename plus required `status`.

findings.narrativeMd: `Account.partOf` was removed from the local Account model and replaced by `Account.parent`. Because FHIR element names are part of the JSON/XML wire format and generated API surface, this is more than a descriptive rename. Any stored R4 Account hierarchy using `partOf` must be transformed before strict R6 validation or ingestion.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances that contain `partOf` can become R6-invalid because `partOf` is no longer a recognized Account element. R6 instances that contain `parent` are not cleanly representable in R4 without converting back to `partOf` or using an extension. Runtime breakage is likely in serializers, generated POCO/POJO classes, FHIRPath rules, indexes, and UI bindings that use the old element name.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Implement an explicit bidirectional transform: R4 `Account.partOf` -> R6 `Account.parent`, and R6 `Account.parent` -> R4 `Account.partOf`. Test records with no parent, a valid parent reference, contained/reference edge cases, and downstream roll-up behavior. Avoid dropping the relationship because it can affect billing account aggregation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The apparent goal could have been achieved less disruptively by keeping `partOf` and improving its definition or by adding `parent` as an optional replacement while retaining `partOf` as deprecated. The tradeoff would be temporary duplicate semantics in the base resource, but it would avoid a hard instance and codegen break.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The mapping is high-confidence because cardinality and target type match exactly; nevertheless, confirm no ballot narrative gives `parent` subtly different semantics before treating the transform as always lossless.

findings.title: Account.description type changed from string to markdown

semanticText.definition: Provides additional information about what the account tracks and how it is used.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 treated Account description as a plain string primitive.

semanticText.definition: Provides additional information about what the account tracks and how it is used.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses the FHIR `markdown` primitive, allowing markdown-formatted narrative while preserving the same element path and cardinality.

facts.note: The wire scalar remains a JSON string, but the FHIR primitive type and generated model type change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON scalar representation remains string-like, so most existing R4 values should continue to parse in R6. The risk is primarily generated-code and semantic rendering: strongly typed models may expose different primitive classes, validators may apply markdown-specific rules, and UI code may render R6 values as markdown instead of plain text.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Description text can influence billing workflow understanding, but this is not itself a coded clinical decision element.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow formatted explanatory text for account purpose/use.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `description` as `string` while documenting that markdown syntax is permitted, or add a separate markdown-capable representation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing formatted explanatory text is a reasonable goal, and using the FHIR `markdown` primitive gives R6 consumers a clear rendering/sanitization signal. The change is mostly a generated-model and semantic break rather than a JSON scalar break, because ordinary R4 string values remain string-shaped.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained the `string` type and clarified that implementations may include markdown syntax in the value. That would preserve most R4 code and instances, but it would not give validators, generated models, or UIs an explicit `markdown` datatype. Adding a parallel markdown field or choice would make the alternative more explicit, but would split one description across competing representations that might never fully converge.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping `string` preserves R4 codegen and wire compatibility but weakens typed markdown semantics; a sibling or choice representation would duplicate one description fact.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example is expected to remain valid in practice; it is included to show the same wire field under a changed primitive type. The R6 markdown example can be carried as an R4 string but may lose intended rendering semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: `Account.description` changed primitive type from `string` to `markdown`. This is unlikely to break ordinary JSON instances because both are represented as strings, but it can break generated models and UI assumptions. R6 producers may include markdown syntax that R4 consumers display literally or sanitize unexpectedly.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Most R4 plain-string descriptions should still be R6-compatible. Potential validation differences depend on primitive datatype rules and terminology/server implementation, so this is marked potential rather than definite hard instance-breaking. R6 markdown content can be represented syntactically as an R4 string, but the markdown semantics are not native to R4 Account.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models and update code that treats `description` as a plain string primitive. For R6-to-R4 conversion, either preserve the markdown source text as a string with documented rendering loss or strip/escape formatting according to consumer policy. Test descriptions with plain text, markdown emphasis/links, and primitive extensions on `_description`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Changing the primitive type in place gives clean R6 semantics but creates codegen churn. A less-breaking approach would have kept `string` and added a markdown extension, but that would make formatted descriptions less visible and less interoperable.

findings.title: Guarantor party is no longer required and guarantor can point to an Account

oldState.summary: Each R4 guarantor required `party` exactly once.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a guarantor backbone element could not be valid without naming a responsible Patient, RelatedPerson, or Organization.

newState.summary: R6 makes `party` optional and adds optional guarantor account, responsibility percentage, financial limit, and rank.

semanticText.comment: A party and/or an account is expected to be present on the guarantor.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows a guarantor entry where `party` is absent, especially when `Account.guarantor.account` supplies a specific Account to use. It also adds financial allocation metadata on the guarantor.

facts.newValue: no computable invariant requiring party or account
facts.note: The R6 comment says party and/or account is expected, but no local invariant was present in the inspected snapshot.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Lowering a minimum cardinality is not an R4-to-R6 validation break. The risk is in the other direction and at runtime: R6 consumers and converters can encounter guarantor rows with no `party`, or with R6-only account/limit/rank/responsibility details. R4 models cannot represent those details natively and R4 business logic often assumes `guarantor.party` is populated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Guarantor responsibility affects payment collection and financial liability; dropping account, rank, limit, or responsibility details can alter billing outcomes.

justification.inferredGoal: Support guarantor responsibility that is tied to another Account and capture ordering, percentage, and financial limits.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: lowering `guarantor.party` from `1..1` to `0..1` and adding optional guarantor details preserves R4-valid Account instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears to be support for account-based guarantor responsibility plus percentage, limit, and rank details. That is a reasonable billing capability, and the base change does not make existing R4 guarantor entries invalid in R6 because R4 entries with `party` remain allowed.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rules this is not a backward-compatible-alternative case: it is a weakening plus optional R6 additions, not an R4-to-R6 base-design break. Keeping `party` mandatory would preserve older runtime assumptions and make R6-to-R4 conversion easier, but it would fail the account-only guarantor use case. A formal `party.exists() or account.exists()` invariant could improve R6 data quality, yet it is not needed to preserve R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The main cost is R6-to-R4 conversion and runtime null-handling; an invariant requiring `party` or `account` would reduce ambiguity but is semantic hardening, not an R4-to-R6 compatibility alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 cardinality is `1..1` with target profiles Patient, RelatedPerson, and Organization.
R6 cardinality is `0..1`; comment says a party and/or account is expected.
evidence.quote: A party and/or an account is expected to be present on the guarantor.

migrationExampleJson.r6ToR4Policy: Map `guarantor.account`, `responsibility`, `limit`, and `rank` to extensions or reject if lossless conversion is required; populate `guarantor.party` only when a real responsible party is known.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment is valid with respect to the inspected Account-specific cardinalities, but it omits `party`, which is invalid in R4.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 widens the guarantor model. `guarantor.party` is no longer mandatory and a guarantor can point to another Account and carry responsibility, limit, and rank. Existing R4 instances remain valid, but R4-era consumers that assume every guarantor has a responsible party can fail or misbill when reading R6 data.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an old-valid/new-invalid change. It is an R6-valid/not-R4-representable pattern: a guarantor without `party`, or with R6-only financial allocation fields, cannot be represented in the R4 base Account resource without extensions or loss. Strict R4 validators reject the new child elements and reject `guarantor` entries missing `party`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, no data repair is required for `party`; existing party references can be preserved. For R6-to-R4, define extensions or a rejection policy for account-only guarantors and for responsibility/limit/rank. Update null-safety in generated-model consumers and add tests for guarantors with party only, account only, both party and account, and neither.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new financial details are useful but the cardinality relaxation weakens a previously reliable invariant. A backward-compatible compromise would have kept party required unless an account was supplied, enforced by an invariant. That would still break R4-to-R6 less than a rename but would better protect consumers from empty guarantor entries.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because the R6 comment uses “expected” rather than a formal constraint, local profiles may need to enforce `party.exists() or account.exists()` if empty guarantors are not meaningful.

findings.title: R6 adds clinical billing context on Account that R4 cannot carry natively

oldState.summary: R4 Account had no native `covers`, `diagnosis`, or `procedure` elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Account could identify subjects, service period, coverage, owner, and guarantors, but it did not directly list covered encounters/episodes or billing diagnoses/procedures.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `covers`, `diagnosis`, and `procedure` structures for episode/encounter coverage and billing-relevant clinical context.

constraints.human: The dateOfDiagnosis is not valid when using a reference to a diagnosis
The dateOfService is not valid when using a reference to a procedure

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can link an Account to Encounter/EpisodeOfCare via `covers`, record billing diagnoses using `diagnosis.condition`, and record billing procedures using `procedure.code`, including local sequencing, type, dates, package codes, present-on-admission, and devices.

facts.note: The new Account-specific invariants restrict date fields when a reference is used.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These are optional additions, so existing R4 Account instances remain valid in R6. The material risk is round-trip and runtime compatibility: R6 producers may put billing diagnoses/procedures and covered encounter/episode links directly on Account. R4 Account has no native fields for those structures, and R4 generated parsers will reject them as unknown.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping diagnoses, procedures, or covered encounter/episode links can affect billing claims, reimbursement logic, and auditability.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent billing-relevant diagnoses/procedures and account episode coverage directly where Account is used for billing workflows.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `covers`, `diagnosis`, and `procedure` are optional R6 additions, so R4 Account instances can remain valid without them.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing billing-relevant encounters, episodes, diagnoses, and procedures on Account is a plausible core R6 goal, and R6 implemented it without requiring new data from existing R4 instances. The breakage described here is mainly for mixed-version consumers and R6-to-R4 round-tripping.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 validation because the new content is optional. Keeping this information solely in extensions, Claim, Encounter, Condition, or Procedure links could preserve the R4 base shape, but that is an alternate modeling or conversion strategy with weaker standardization, not a backward-compatible alternative to an actual R4-to-R6 break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Base elements standardize common billing context for R6 but create R6-to-R4 representability gaps; extensions or related-resource mappings are migration/down-conversion strategies rather than backward-compatible base alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 adds mandatory `diagnosis.condition` within each diagnosis as `CodeableReference(Condition)`.
R6 adds mandatory `procedure.code` within each procedure as `CodeableReference(Procedure)`.
R4 Account has no `covers`, `diagnosis`, or `procedure` elements.

migrationExampleJson.r6ToR4Policy: Represent these fields with extensions, map to related Claim/Encounter/Condition/Procedure resources where a receiving workflow supports that, or reject lossless R6-to-R4 conversion.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates R6-only Account content. A full migration must also respect the R6 `act-1` and `act-2` invariants around date fields when references are used.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 Account can now directly carry billing-relevant clinical context. This is a major expressivity increase, not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but it is material for converters and mixed-version deployments because R4 Account has no equivalent base elements.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid because the new elements are optional. R6 instances using these elements are not R4-representable without extensions, related-resource transforms, or data loss. New R6 invariants also mean that, within R6, diagnosis/procedure date fields are invalid when a reference form is used for the corresponding CodeableReference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, leave these fields absent unless billing data can be derived from local systems or related resources. For R6-to-R4, decide whether to use extensions, map to Claim/Encounter/Condition/Procedure, or reject records requiring lossless conversion. Test CodeableReference concept-only and reference forms, date constraints, multiple sequence values, and device-linked procedures.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are the least disruptive way to add this R6 capability for forward validation, but they necessarily create R6-to-R4 representability gaps. Keeping all content as extensions would have reduced cross-version base-model differences but at the cost of weaker standardization.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact best mapping may depend on whether a workflow treats Account as pre-Claim billing context or derives these details from Claim/Encounter resources.

findings.title: R6 adds Account billing status, currency, balance, and calculation timestamp

oldState.summary: R4 Account had no native billing lifecycle status, default currency, calculated balances, or balance calculation timestamp elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Account identified and described an account but did not carry structured current/aged balance snapshots or a separate billing lifecycle status.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `billingStatus`, `currency`, repeating `balance`, and `calculatedAt` fields.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: `billingStatus` uses an example binding to `ValueSet/account-billing-status`; `currency` has a required binding to ISO 4217 currencies; `balance.aggregate` and `balance.term` have extensible bindings to new R6 Account value sets.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 Account can express billing workflow state, default currency, one or more balance amounts by aggregate/term/estimate, and when those balances were calculated.

impact.impactRationaleMd: All of these elements are optional at the Account level, so existing R4 data is not invalidated. R6 producers can, however, include financial state that R4 Account cannot represent. Dropping balances, currency, or billing status can change business behavior and audit results.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Currency and balance information directly affect financial calculations and patient/guarantor billing responsibilities; loss or misinterpretation can have high business impact.

justification.inferredGoal: Support Account as a financial/billing object with explicit billing lifecycle and balance snapshots.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: billing status, currency, balance, and calculated-at fields are optional R6 additions and do not invalidate R4 Account instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Structured billing lifecycle, currency, balance, and calculation timestamp data are natural Account capabilities for financial systems. Because R6 adds them optionally, the design preserves forward validation for R4 instances while increasing expressivity for R6 producers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This is not a backward-compatible-alternative issue under the calibration rules because the finding is about optional R6-only content and down-conversion risk. Extensions or a separate finance resource could be used as migration or alternate modeling approaches, but they are not evidence that a less-breaking base design was required for R4-to-R6 compatibility.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 data loss or extension use for populated financial fields; avoiding base fields would reduce down-conversion gaps but weaken R6 standardization of financial state.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `billingStatus` as `0..1 CodeableConcept` with example binding to `ValueSet/account-billing-status`.
R6 adds `currency` as `0..1 CodeableConcept` with required binding to `ValueSet/currencies|6.0.0-ballot4`.
R6 adds repeating `balance` where each balance requires `amount 1..1` of type Money.
R4 Account has no `billingStatus`, `currency`, `balance`, or `calculatedAt` elements.
R6 includes new Account billing/balance code systems and uses ISO 4217 currencies for the required currency binding.

migrationExampleJson.r6ToR4Policy: Use extensions for billingStatus/currency/balance/calculatedAt, or drop with explicit data-loss annotation; do not silently ignore financial amounts in lossless workflows.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment shows financial fields that a strict R4 Account parser will not accept as base elements.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a structured financial snapshot to Account. This is useful for billing systems but a significant down-conversion issue because R4 Account has no native fields for billing lifecycle, default currency, aged/current balances, or calculation timestamp.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Existing R4 Account instances remain R6-valid because the new fields are optional. R6 instances that populate them are not valid R4 base Account instances. The required binding on `currency` matters only when R6 `currency` is present; `balance.amount` is mandatory only inside a present `balance` repetition.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not silently discard populated R6 financial fields in R6-to-R4 conversion unless the workflow explicitly tolerates loss. Prefer cross-version extensions for lossless storage, or map to local finance models outside FHIR Account. Validate ISO currency codings, `Money.currency` consistency, balance term/aggregate values, and stale `calculatedAt` handling.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional base additions were backward-compatible for R4-to-R6 validation. The unavoidable cost is R6-to-R4 representability. Extensions would have reduced base-model change but weakened standard support for common financial data.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A terminology-server expansion would improve confidence for the external ISO 4217 currency value set, but the presence and binding strength are clear from the local StructureDefinition.

findings.title: Account.subject guidance now allows billing-demographic Patient divergence from clinical Patient

oldState.summary: R4 subject comment only described non-patient and unallocated account use cases.

semanticText.definition: Identifies the entity which incurs the expenses. While the immediate recipients of services or goods might be entities related to the subject, the expenses were ultimately incurred by the subject of the Account.
semanticText.comment: Accounts can be applied to non-patients for tracking other non-patient related activities, such as group services (patients not tracked, and costs charged to another body), or might not be allocated.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not explicitly discuss using a different Patient resource for billing demographics than the Patient used by clinical resources.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same cardinality and target types, but adds guidance permitting Account to reference a different Patient instance for billing demographics and recommending `Patient.link` type `seealso`.

semanticText.definition: Identifies the entity which incurs the expenses. While the immediate recipients of services or goods might be entities related to the subject, the expenses were ultimately incurred by the subject of the Account.
semanticText.comment: Accounts might reference a different Patient resource instance than is referenced by clinical resources if the demographics for the Account differ from the demographics that are most appropriate for clinical purposes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 explicitly documents a billing-demographics pattern where Account.subject may intentionally differ from the clinical Patient resource and the two Patients should be linked.

facts.oldValue: No explicit billing-demographics Patient divergence guidance.
facts.newValue: Account may reference a different Patient than clinical resources and should link Patient instances using Patient.link type seealso.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No validation shape changed, but R6 changes the conformance story around identity assumptions. Systems that infer the Account patient must equal the Encounter/clinical-resource patient may make incorrect joins or reject valid R6 usage where billing and clinical demographics are represented by linked but distinct Patient resources.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect patient identity assumptions can affect billing, privacy, and record-linking workflows, although the guidance is not a direct validation rule.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify billing-demographics use cases where payer-facing demographics differ from clinical-care demographics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the `subject` cardinality and reference targets are unchanged, and the change is explanatory guidance rather than an R4-to-R6 validation break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying that billing demographics may require a different linked Patient resource is a reasonable conformance goal, and it was accomplished without changing the Account.subject wire shape. The compatibility risk is behavioral for systems with stricter local assumptions, not a base instance-validity break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because no R4 Account instance becomes invalid and no R6-only field is introduced on `subject`, there is no backward-compatible base alternative to assess. Keeping the shorter R4 comment and moving the billing-demographics discussion to narrative or implementation-guide text could reduce generated-documentation churn, but it would also make the intended semantics easier to miss.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Inline guidance improves discoverability but may require review of local patient-identity assumptions; narrative-only guidance would be less visible, not a compatibility-preserving base alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 comment discusses non-patient accounts and unallocated accounts, without the billing-vs-clinical Patient divergence guidance.
R6 adds guidance that Account may reference a different Patient resource instance than clinical resources and recommends Patient.link type `seealso`.
evidence.quote: Accounts might reference a different Patient resource instance than is referenced by clinical resources if the demographics for the Account differ from the demographics that are most appropriate for clinical purposes.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is structurally valid in R4 and R6; the risk is semantic. A complete R6 example would include the clinical Patient and `Patient.link` relationship outside Account.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds explicit guidance that Account.subject can point to a Patient resource optimized for billing demographics rather than the Patient used for clinical care, with Patient.link connecting the records. This does not break validation, but it can break implicit business rules and joins.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no old-valid/new-invalid structural change and no native R6-to-R4 wire incompatibility for the `subject` element itself. Compatibility risk is behavioral: systems may treat a changed Account.subject Patient as a data-quality error or may join billing and clinical records incorrectly.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review local Account, Encounter, Claim, and Patient matching logic. Do not assume Account.subject Patient must equal Encounter.subject Patient. Add tests for linked but distinct billing and clinical Patient records, and decide how to expose this in user interfaces and privacy/audit workflows.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the element shape did not change, this is a low-disruption way to clarify semantics. The backward-compatible alternative would be narrative-only guidance, but that would be easier to miss and less useful to implementers reading generated element documentation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confidence is medium rather than high for impact because this is a comment-level semantic change; actual breakage depends on local business rules.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag remain aligned. The StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active, which is notable but not an identity break.

No local Account element minimum cardinality increased and no existing local maximum cardinality was narrowed. The only existing local cardinality change found was `Account.guarantor.party` decreasing from `1..1` to `0..1`, which is covered as an R6-to-R4/runtime risk rather than an R4-to-R6 hard break.

Existing local reference target lists checked for `subject`, `coverage.coverage`, `owner`, and `guarantor.party` did not narrow. `partOf` to `parent` keeps `Reference(Account)` and is covered separately as a rename.

The required `Account.status` binding remains required and the local R4/R6 account-status CodeSystems contain the same five codes: `active`, `inactive`, `entered-in-error`, `on-hold`, and `unknown`. New bindings on added R6 elements are covered in findings. No terminology-server expansion was run for external value sets.

No existing local Account-specific constraint was removed or strengthened. New Account-specific constraints `act-1` and `act-2` apply only to new R6 diagnosis/procedure backbone elements and are covered with those additions. Inherited `ele-1`, `ext-1`, and DomainResource constraints were excluded as base-artifact changes.
Existing local modifier semantics were stable: `Account.status` remains a modifier and no existing local Account element became a modifier or stopped being one.
No Account-specific slicing changes were identified in the compared snapshots/differentials.
No Account-specific fixed, pattern, or default value changes were identified.
No Account-specific maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were identified on existing local elements.

No existing local Account element had a material summary flag change. Several new R6 elements such as `billingStatus`, `covers`, `diagnosis`, and `procedure` are summary elements; that matters for R6 `_summary` behavior and is noted in the addition findings.

No representation-format change was found other than the local `partOf`/`parent` wire-name change and `description` primitive type change, both covered as findings. XML/RDF-specific serialization details were not independently tested.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The artifact identity and content model correspondence remain direct; status maturity affects governance expectations rather than instance validity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat the R6 Account definition as more mature/active in conformance planning, but do not migrate instance data solely because of this status change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Account.status required value set version changed but code list stayed the same in local artifacts
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both local AccountStatus CodeSystems contain `active`, `inactive`, `entered-in-error`, `on-hold`, and `unknown`; no code removal or addition was found for the required binding.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Update canonical version references from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4` where tooling pins the value set version, but enum switches over the base codes should not need code-list changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Most new R6 Account elements are optional
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The added Account elements have Account-level minimum cardinality `0`, so R4 instances are not forced to populate new data for R6 validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Forward migrations may leave new R6 fields empty, but product teams should decide whether to enrich them from local billing systems.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Common inherited resource changes, including language binding/comment/constraint differences visible on Account snapshots, were excluded and should be handled by the DomainResource/Resource base-artifact analysis.
Inherited `ele-1`, `ext-1`, extension text, and backbone child behavior appear in Account snapshots but are not local Account changes.
R6 adds financial terminology bindings. A terminology-focused review/expansion would improve confidence for implementers relying on strict code validation and mappings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 Account diff, Jira ticket, or ballot rationale was supplied, so justification and backward-compatible alternative assessments are inferred from the computable artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the rendered R6 Account change history, ballot reconciliation notes, or HL7 Jira items for Account.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology checks used local ValueSet and CodeSystem compose/content. No live expansion was run for external systems such as ISO 4217 or v3 ActCode.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology-server expansions for the relevant R4 and R6 value sets and compare expanded code sets.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis did not inspect rendered specification pages, examples, or implementation notes that may explain intended mappings for new R6 Account billing fields.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the R6 ballot Account narrative page, examples, and any cross-version mapping guidance.
